sentences.text: 3.  The brief fact of the case is that the petitioner is an accused of Govindpur P.S. Case No. 27 of 2019, corresponding to G.R. No. 1328 of 2018 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 494, 313 of Indian Penal Code and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

During the pendency of the said case, there was a compromise between the petitioner and the opposite party no.2 and consequent upon that the petitioner was given the privilege of anticipatory bail vide A.B.P. No. 514 of 2018 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur and the major condition of the same was that the petitioner will keep and maintain the opposite party no.2 with full dignity and honour as his lawful wife.

Thereafter, the opposite party no.2 filed Cr.
Misc. Petition No.04 of 2019 in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC,
Jamshedpur for cancellation of the bail granted to the petitioner.
4. The Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur cancelled the bail of the petitioner for the reason that he has violated the condition of the bail.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that after settlement of the dispute, the father of the opposite party no.2 namely Satyendra Saw gave an undertaking on 24.02.2018 that he is taking his daughter to his house for a week and he will bring back the opposite party no.2 after ten days but did not bring back the opposite party no.2 and instead got Sitaramdera P.S. Case No.23 of 2019 registered alleging commission of the offence punishable under Section 498A/34 of Indian Penal Code.
It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner filed A.B.A. No. 4033 of 2019.

Notices was issued to the opposite party no.2 and the opposite party no.2 through her Advocate appeared and intimated the Court that she is not ready and willing to resume conjugal life with the petitioner and consequent upon that the petitioner was given the privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Sitaramdera P.S. Case No. 23 of 2019.

It is then submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC,
Jamshedpur failed to consider that there is no violation of any terms and condition on the part of the petitioner rather the opposite party no.2 is not ready and willing to resume conjugal life with the petitioner and the petitioner has not committed any wrong for which the bail granted to him in terms of the order passed in A.B.P. No. 514 of 2018 be cancelled.
Hence, it is submitted that the order dated 29.01.2021 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur being not sustainable in law be quashed and set aside.

6. Learned Special Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand opposes the prayer for quashing the order dated 29.01.2021 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur.

It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 that the petitioner started violating the terms and condition of the compromise and has solemnized marriage with Babita Kumar and committed the offence punishable under Section 494 of Indian Penal Code.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

sentences.text:
Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law that the grounds for which the bail granted to the accused person of a case can be cancelled illustratively though not exhaustively are as under:-
(i) by indulging in similar criminal activity,
(ii) interfering with the course of investigation,
(iii) attempted to tamper with evidence or witnesses,
(iv) threaten witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper smooth investigation,
(v) there is likelihood of their fleeing to another country,
(vi) attempted to make themselves scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency,
(vii) attempted to place themselves beyond the reach of his surety, etc.
8.

It is also a settled principle of law as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Pritpal Singh Vs. State of Bihar reported in 2001 SCC OnLine SC 123 paragraphs-4 & 5 of which read as under:-
4.

entities.text: Pritpal Singh Vs. State of Bihar reported in 2001 SCC OnLine SC 123
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The dispute raised in the case relates to eviction of the appellant who is the tenant from the premises of which the respondent is the owner.
Previously, there was a compromise between the parties in which it was agreed inter alia that the appellant will pay certain amount to the respondent and vacate the premises by the time stipulated.

On the allegation that the appellant has failed to comply with the terms of the compromise by not vacating the premises in question within the time stipulated,
the petition for cancellation of bail was filed.

It is stated by learned counsel for the appellant that neither was any averment made in the petition about misuse of liberty granted to the appellant nor was any difficulty alleged to have been faced by the prosecution in the case on the ground of the appellant being at large.
5. The Magistrate cancelled the bail granted to the appellant solely on the ground that the terms of the compromise had not been complied with.
To say the least, the ground on which the petition for cancellation of bail was made and was granted is wholly untenable.
It is our view that the order if allowed to stand will result in abuse of the process of court.
The High Court clearly erred in maintaining the order.
Therefore, the order passed by the Magistrate cancelling the bail and the order of the High Court confirming the said order are set aside.
The bail order is restored.
The appeal is allowed."

sentences.text: 9. Now coming to the facts of the case, it is evident from the order dated 02.09.2019 passed in A.B.A. No. 4033 of 2019 in connection with Sitaramdera P.S. Case No. 23 of 2019 that the opposite party no.2 is not ready and willing to resume conjugal life with the petitioner because of his past conduct.
When the opposite party no.2 is not ready and willing to resume conjugal life with the petitioner, there is no way the petitioner could do the same.

10. It is a settled principle of law that the object underlying the cancellation of bail is to protect the fair trial and secure justice being done to the society by preventing the accused who is set at liberty by the bail order from tampering with evidence as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Panchanan Mishra vs. Digambar Mishra & Ors. reported in (2005) 3 SCC 143.

sentences.text:
It is also a settled principle of law that the court cannot cancel the bail on a ground alien to the grounds mentioned under Section 437 of Code of Criminal Procedure as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Biman Chatterjee vs. Sanchita Chatterjee & Anr.
reported in (2004) 3 SCC 388.
11.

reported in (2004) 3 SCC 388
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now coming to the facts of the case, there is no allegation against the petitioner of having committed any of the acts, deeds or thing which could have made him liable for cancellation of the bail as mentioned above.

12. As already mentioned above, since the opposite party no.2 is not ready and willing to resume conjugal life with the petitioner, no fault could be found with the petitioner for not resuming conjugal life with the opposite party no.2.
13.

Under such circumstances, this Court has no hesitation in holding that the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur has committed perversity in cancelling the bail granted to the petitioner.
14.
Accordingly the order dated 29.01.2021 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-FTC, Jamshedpur is quashed and set aside.
15. The bail of the petitioner granted to him in connection with Govindpur P.S. Case No. 27 of 2018 is restored.
16. In the result, this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.
